sections.title: Emilia-Romagna & Northern Italy: Culture, Cuisine & Historic Cities
sections.subtitle: Introduction
sections.html:
Emilia-Romagna & Northern Italy: Culture, Cuisine & Historic Cities

Journey through the heart of Emilia-Romagna and Northern Italy, exploring vibrant cities, medieval villages, and UNESCO World Heritage sites. Discover the region’s rich culture, renowned cuisine, and historic landmarks, from Bologna’s lively markets to Parma’s culinary traditions and Verona’s romantic streets.

sections.title: Day 1 - Classic Bologna & Gastronomy
sections.html:
Arrival at Bologna Airport

Arrival at Bologna Airport, where the group will be welcomed by a French-speaking tour escort.

Private coach transfer to central Bologna

Private coach transfer to central Bologna.

Guided tour of Bologna’s historic center

The day is dedicated to discovering Bologna’s culture and cuisine. Meet your local guide for a visit to Piazza Maggiore, the historic heart of Bologna for centuries, surrounded by the city’s most important civic landmarks: Palazzo d’Accursio, Palazzo Re Enzo, Palazzo del Podestà, the magnificent Basilica of San Petronio, Neptune Fountain, Palazzo dei Notai, and Palazzo de’ Banchi. Visit the Archiginnasio Palace and its historic Anatomical Theatre (interior visit).

Explore medieval market and Loggia dei Mercanti

Continue through the lively, narrow streets of the historic center to the old medieval market and the 14th-century Loggia dei Mercanti, which still retains its Gothic charm. The tour concludes at Bologna’s famous Two Towers, iconic monuments dating to the Middle Ages.

Traditional lunch at a restaurant

Enjoy a traditional lunch at a restaurant.

Afternoon guided tour of historic Bolognese shops

In the afternoon, continue the guided tour through historic Bolognese shops filled with stories, anecdotes, and legends, many preserving decorative details from earlier eras. Sample several local specialties along the way.

Return to hotel for dinner and overnight

Return to the hotel in the evening for dinner and overnight accommodation.

sections.title: Day 2 - Parmigiano Reggiano, Parma & Historic Center
sections.html:
Breakfast at the hotel

Breakfast at the hotel.

Depart for Parmigiano Reggiano producer

Depart for an artisanal producer of the famous Italian Parmigiano Reggiano cheese, described as the only producer of vintage-aged and kosher Parmigiano Reggiano.

Guided tour of Parmigiano Reggiano production

Take a guided tour of the production facilities and aging warehouse. An expert will explain the stages of cheesemaking, from milk processing to maturation.

Parmigiano Reggiano tasting

Enjoy a comparative tasting of Parmigiano Reggiano aged 15, 24, and 36 months, accompanied by toast with a special Parmesan cream, a platter of PDO Parma ham, and a glass of Lambrusco and Malvasia wine.

Continue to Parma for lunch

Continue to Parma for lunch at a restaurant. Parma is one of Italy’s most attractive cultural and culinary destinations, celebrated for its monuments, castles, art, cuisine, and opera.

Lunch at a restaurant in Parma

Lunch at a restaurant in Parma.

Explore Parma’s historic center

Explore the historic center, including Piazza del Duomo, the Cathedral and Baptistery (interior visits), Piazza Garibaldi, the renowned Teatro Regio, the Church of Santa Maria della Steccata, and the Farnese Theatre (interior visit).

Free time in Parma

Free time before returning to the hotel for dinner and overnight accommodation.

Return to hotel

Return to the hotel for dinner and overnight accommodation.

Dinner at the hotel

Dinner at the hotel.

Traditional lunch at the agriturismo La Locanda del Mulino in Castelvetro.

In the afternoon, enjoy guided visits to the historic villages of Castelvetro and Vignola, viewing their monuments from the outside.

sections.title: Day 4 - Parma Ham, Modena and Balsamic Vinegar
sections.html:
Breakfast at the hotel

Breakfast at the hotel.

Depart for Langhirano to visit Parma ham producer

Depart for Langhirano to visit an artisanal Parma ham producer. Learn about the various stages of the famous ham’s curing and maturation process.

Visit to Parma ham producer

Learn about the various stages of the famous ham’s curing and maturation process. The visit concludes with a tasting lunch featuring products from the salumificio (cured-meat producer).

Tasting lunch at the salumificio

The visit concludes with a tasting lunch featuring products from the salumificio (cured-meat producer).

Return to Modena for guided tour

Return to Modena for a guided tour of its historic center, including the 12th-century Romanesque Cathedral, part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997 (interior visit), the impressive rooms of City Hall, the majestic Ducal Palace, and the city’s beautiful churches.

Guided tour of Modena historic center

Guided tour of Modena's historic center, including the 12th-century Romanesque Cathedral (interior visit), City Hall, Ducal Palace, and beautiful churches.

Visit to traditional balsamic vinegar producer

At the end of the excursion, visit a traditional balsamic vinegar producer and enjoy a tasting on site.

Return to hotel

Return to the hotel for dinner and overnight accommodation.

sections.title: Day 5 - Ferrara and Comacchio Exploration
sections.html:
Breakfast at the hotel

Breakfast at the hotel.

Depart for Ferrara

Depart for Ferrara, a city of the Po Valley shaped over the centuries by the Po River and closely linked to its waterways.

Guided walk through Ferrara historic center

Enjoy a guided walk through the historic center, featuring Palazzo dei Diamanti, Estense Castle, the magnificent Romanesque-origin Cathedral, the Jewish Ghetto, and the medieval quarter.

Lunch at a restaurant

Lunch at a restaurant.

Continue to Comacchio

Continue to Comacchio, a picturesque town in the Po Delta often compared to Venice for its canals, bridges, and 17th- and 18th-century houses.

Explore Comacchio historic center

See the famous Trepponti bridge, the Cathedral of San Cassiano, elegant Palazzo Bellini, Piazza Maggiore, and the Loggia dei Mercanti with its striking portico (exterior views).

Return to hotel

Return to the hotel in the evening for dinner and overnight accommodation.

Dinner at the hotel.

sections.title: Day 6 - Verona’s Roman Arena and Historic Center
sections.html:
Breakfast at the hotel

Breakfast at the hotel.

Depart for Verona

Depart for the Veneto region and arrive in Verona by midmorning. Elegant and romantic Verona is famous worldwide as the setting of Romeo and Juliet. Its UNESCO-listed historic center reflects more than 2,000 years of history. One of its best-known landmarks is the Roman Arena, among the best-preserved ancient amphitheaters in the world and still used for opera and performances.

Walking tour of Verona historic center

Meet your guide for a walking tour of the historic center, including Piazza Bra and the Arena, elegant Via Mazzini, Piazza delle Erbe, Piazza dei Signori, Juliet’s House and its famous balcony, and the picturesque Ponte Pietra over the Adige River (exterior views).

Lunch at a restaurant

Lunch at a restaurant, followed by free time to explore Verona independently.

Return to Modena

Return to Modena in the evening for dinner and overnight accommodation.

sections.title: Day 7 - Piacenza and Castell’Arquato Exploration
sections.html:
Breakfast at the hotel

Breakfast at the hotel.

Depart for Piacenza

Depart for Piacenza, an elegant art city in the heart of Emilia-Romagna.

Walking tour of Piacenza historic center

Meet a local guide for a walking tour of the historic center, including Piazza Cavalli, the Gothic Palace, and the Cathedral, an outstanding example of Romanesque architecture. The tour offers insight into local history, culture, and traditions (exterior views of monuments).

Lunch at a restaurant

Lunch at a restaurant.

Continue to Castell’Arquato

Continue to Castell’Arquato, considered one of the region’s most beautiful medieval villages.

Guided stroll through Castell’Arquato

Stroll with your guide through picturesque lanes and admire its exceptionally well-preserved heritage, including small squares, old stairways, and medieval towers.

Return to hotel

Return to the hotel in the evening for dinner and overnight accommodation.

sections.title: Day 8 - Ravenna and Brisighella Discovery
sections.subtitle: 11-May-2027
sections.html:
Breakfast at the hotel

Breakfast at the hotel.

Depart for Ravenna

Depart for Ravenna, once the capital of the Western Roman Empire, later of the Ostrogothic Kingdom and Byzantine Italy. The city is renowned for its extraordinary UNESCO-listed mosaics.

Guided exploration of Ravenna historic center

Meet your guide to explore the historic center and its principal monuments. Visit the Basilica of San Vitale, known for its octagonal architecture and exceptionally refined Byzantine mosaics. Continue to the Mausoleum of Galla Placidia, whose modest exterior conceals a spectacular interior of deep-blue mosaics and a peaceful atmosphere. Visit the Basilica of Sant’Apollinare Nuovo, celebrated for its long mosaic processions of saints and virgins. Stop outside the tomb of the Italian poet Dante Alighieri.

Lunch at a restaurant

Lunch at a restaurant.

Continue to Brisighella

Continue to Brisighella, a charming medieval village nestled in the hills.

Free time in Brisighella

Enjoy free time to discover its narrow lanes, stone houses, and three famous hills crowned by the Rocca fortress, Clock Tower, and Sanctuary of Monticino.

Return to hotel

Return to the hotel in the evening.

Upgraded four-course dinner at the hotel

Enjoy an upgraded four-course dinner at the hotel, or optionally at Europa 92 restaurant for an additional charge.
